title: Mary Magdalene in the garden (John 20:1–18)
hookLine: she thinks he's the gardener until he says her name
last: GOD IS IN THE SILENCE TOO.

lines: A NAME, SAID BY SOMEONE WHO KNOWS YOU.
cards: A name is a strange thing. A stranger reads it off a list and it's just a word. Someone who knows you says it once, quietly, across a crowded room, and it lands differently.
Early on the first day of the week, while it's still dark, Mary Magdalene walks to the tomb. The stone has been rolled away. The body is gone.
She runs for Peter; they come, look, and go home. She stays outside the tomb, crying.

teach.b: She bends to look in and sees two angels, who ask why she's weeping. They've taken my Lord away, she says, and I don't know where they've laid him. She turns, and a man is standing there.
In the Douay-Rheims he asks: "Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou?" She thinks he's the gardener. Sir, she says, if you've moved him, tell me where, and I'll take him.
Then he says one word. "Mary." Not a proof.

teach.h: KNOWN BY HER NAME, NOT HIS FACE.
teach.b: Her name. And she turns and says: "Rabboni," which John explains means Master, my teacher. Notice the Gospel's honesty: she doesn't recognize the risen Jesus by his face.
She knows him by the way he says her name. Then he sends her: go to my brothers, and tell them. She goes to the disciples and says: "I have seen the Lord."
In John's Gospel she is the first to see him risen, sent to tell the ones who will tell everyone else.
The Church calls her the apostle to the apostles, and in 2016 Pope Francis raised her day, 22 July, to a feast, like the apostles' own.
One more thing to clear up. Later preaching called her a repentant prostitute. The Gospels never say that.
It came from sermons, Pope Gregory the Great's among them, that blended her with other women in the Gospels, and the Church's calendar separated them again in 1969.

how: Catholics hear John's account of Mary Magdalene at the tomb on Easter Sunday morning, and keep her feast on 22 July as the apostle to the apostles.

games.q: you're Mary Magdalene. a man you think is the gardener asks why you're crying. what do you say?
o: if you've moved him, tell me where, and I'll take him.
call for the others to come back.
games.why: she asks the 'gardener' where he's laid the body. then he says, "Mary," and she knows him.

practice: Bring to mind someone who says your name the way it's meant to be said, a grandparent, a friend, someone who has known you for years, and hear it in their voice, once. Christians believe God knows each person by name, like that.
If you pray, you can sit quietly and imagine your name said with that kind of love.

wordCard.voice: Rabboni. What Mary Magdalene called Jesus the moment she heard him say her name outside the empty tomb.

orig.note: an Aramaic word kept in the Greek Gospel: my master, my teacher. what she says when she knows him.

carryVoice: Your line: he says your name. She knew him by it, not by his face. See you tomorrow.
